scope: The three certificate wrappers only, with adjacent output-law, support, Good/Certificate, finish and charge definitions inspected. No fresh compiler or independent reproof of the interpreter/quality dependencies.
findings: Both executePrefix definitions return the entire (output, ledger) pair and discard only the remaining bit-list state at this wrapper boundary. Validity, selected quality and cumulative charges refer to that one execution, retaining their correlations.

Pathwise validity and declared charges use the actual support theorem for every supplied finite list, including empty and exhausted lists. This does not assert a fair output distribution for an arbitrary fixed or undersized list.

The confidence theorems use the exact independent finite-prefix law at the proved whole-program budget, then a pushforward equality for the complete output/ledger. Constants precede graph size, input, confidence and entering ledger. No independence between quality and cost, nor between selected output and ledger, is introduced.

Ready and weighted charge proofs separate actual preparation branches. The nonempty heavy branch pays preparation, original weighted query, combined-mask work and final overhead; the zero-residual branch is treated directly. The cumulative operation identity and deterministic declared envelope hold on all supported outcomes, including bad-quality outputs.

FiniteHeavyCertificate.Good retains original-cut validity, the established uniform K*n^(1/3+delta) quality factor, the actual cumulative sampler-charge equality and the declared whole-query envelope. Failure is bounded by 2^(-k) with extra=3*k.
qualifications: Outer adaptive packing composition, materializing raw rational inputs/fuel/prefix, physical storage and physical-machine runtime remain outside these wrappers.
Operation counts are the existing declared annotated-operation model, not measured host runtime.
The metadata file still records its draft stage; this review does not turn pending kernel replay into a passed gate.
